P522, that's the burning of the residence of the UNMOs. Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, there is also evidence, and if we go to P525, that other houses were burning on the 6th of August, when you were at times, I understand, swimming in the lake, on the road Gracac-Stikada, with a visible plume of smoke. So that's the road Gracac-Stikada. Did you, did your reconnaissance group, did anybody from your policemen, observe this house burning, this plume of smoke?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we can go to the next example, P526, again a burning house observed on the 6th of August. And this one is slightly more south of Gracac, and I'll show the location in a second. Do you remember having seen this house or the smoke?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go to the map, which is P536. That's a larger map of Gracac, and you'll see the location of this house in -- if you focus on the center, the word "Gracac." You go about a hand into the direction of 7.00 on the clock, and you see the word "Gacese." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's the location of this house, and I think your units were on the left of this map, in those areas where the lake was. So, again, nobody from your police unit, no sentries, no members swimming, nobody saw smoke coming off these houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Just briefly on these combat check-points, "BPP" in your language, can you tell us who manned these combat check-points?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were members of the Varazdin Special Police Unit there, normally between three and four policemen, depending on the commander's assessment, what the required manning levels were. They had short and long barrels. Those closer to the road also had anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And they were focusing apparently on -- primarily on the roads. That's where you, I take it, anticipated some tank approaching. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some check-points that were close to the road. Nevertheless, we had descended from Velebit, and there was a bit of forest near the lake, so there was some check-points inside the forest. We didn't know exactly where the enemy was, and we found it rather strange that there was no one around in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the check-points would be operational located there as long as the Special Police units were there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also told us that on the 7th of August, you were moving on the road from the Gracac area to Bruvno and Lapac, and that, I understand, at least in relation to Mazin, which is north of Bruvno, you did not use the asphalt road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. As far as I remember, a segment of the route was an asphalt road, but we left all of our vehicles at a plateau in Kriste [phoen] and then continued to walk toward the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But I understand that there was at least one vehicle that followed you on the asphalt road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was an APC that we had with us as support.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, we had a witness here testifying that there was a large amount of houses along the road between Gracac and Donji Lapac burnt down or destroyed, and you saw members of the Special Police present in the area while the dwellings were still ablaze. And, Mr. President, that's Witness 82, statement P2359. Now, do you have any personal knowledge of that damage, or did you get reports from reconnaissance groups, or perhaps from the members of this APC who was travelling at least part of that road?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anything, myself, and we got no reports from our reconnaissance groups. When we travelled through that village, everything seemed fine, and there were no fires there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's move to Donji Lapac. In your witness statement, in paragraph 5 and 6, you describe reaching Donji Lapac at around 1.00. Now, did your whole unit of, I think, approximately 120 to 140 people enter Donji Lapac at that time, around 1.00?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, your live testimony about your stay in Donji Lapac, how long you stayed there, is not very detailed, so let me have a look at paragraph 7 of your witness statement, which is D1893. And you said -- as a starting point, you say here that: "We stayed in the area of Donji Lapac until after noon, when the Croatian Army entered." Now, did you personally see the Croatian Army entering into Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you get in touch with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did somebody else from your unit get in touch with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's go to your commander's report, P1237. In English, it's on page 3, and in Croatian, it's, I think, the third electronic page, which is real page 16. In English, it reads as follows, the second paragraph on page 3: "The Special Police forces entered Donji Lapac at 2.00, where they immediately got in touch with the UNCRO." And you talked about that in your testimony. And then, the next paragraph, last sentence: "At 1930 hours on the said day, the HV 118th Home Guard Regiment Brigade arrived from the direction of Udbine, and we established contact." Perhaps for the benefit of the witness, if we could go in Croatian to, I think, the third electronic page. Yes, that's 16. At half past 7.00, met 118th Home Guard Regiment Brigade, and "we established contact with them." That's what your commander wrote in this report. You were not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When they approached, I had to re-deploy our own unit and move them further towards the edges, and then we set up combat check-points. I only spotted them when they were at a distance of about 500 metres from Donji Lapac. At this point in time, we weren't even sure whether those were our soldiers or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But you accept that apparently your commander has gotten in touch with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I didn't see that happen, myself. He may have seen them, but we had no point of contact with them or, indeed, any obligation to get in touch. If there were any further contacts with them, I'm sure it was something that people from our own staff were in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Why do you say it's possible if it's written here? It's a fact that your commander established contact with them. Are you denying --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As I said, I didn't see it, myself, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Incidentally, if you know, when was this report, drafted by your commander, drafted?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was drafted following Operation Storm, some days after. I can't say exactly how many. Maybe a week or two later, when the Special Police Sector requested that we submit our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And were you involved in drafting, were you requested input, or was it the commander, himself, who did it, perhaps with the help of others?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did it with someone else's assistance. I wasn't there when the report was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know who else assisted him, your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I left. I was on leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let's move on to what happened afterwards. And you just, in response to my question, again said that you moved on with at least part of your unit. And in your witness statement, again in paragraph 7, the very end of your statement, you say that: "Afterwards, we took our unit from Donji Lapac to a nearby town, where we spent a night." Which one was this nearby town? What's the name of it?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the -- it was a fringe area of Lapac, itself. It was a hamlet belonging to Donji Lapac. I can't remember the name of the hamlet. We had the forest to our left, and the rest I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't know what the Croatian original says, but "town" is completely different to a hamlet for me. I've been looking for this nearby town to Donji Lapac. Can we actually have a look at D1893, paragraph 7. In kilometres or metres, how far away from the center of Donji Lapac was this hamlet?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say, but about a kilometre from the center of Donji Lapac. It was, however, part of Donji Lapac, a street further out, something like that. It was part of Donji Lapac, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, about the town, isn't that location in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That might be one of the changes from my early version. Nearby location, yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, while you were at that hamlet outside Donji Lapac, did you realise, during the night hours, what was happening in -- or did you observe what was happening in Donji Lapac, itself? Do you have any knowledge of activities in Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any knowledge of the activities there. I know what we were ordered by our commander. We were to prepare and then press on the next morning. As for what was going on in Lapac, based on what we could hear, there was a lot of firing going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say: "On 8th of August, we handed our position over to the Croatian Army and returned to our base in Varazdin." Yes, that appears also in the current translation. Now, to whom did you turn over your positions? Do you know the name of the unit, or perhaps the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I don't remember the commander's name. The unit was deployed on a reserve attack position, but it was never used. We were leaving the area, and I think there was a home guard regiment of some kind; the 118th, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's turn to an issue you discussed in your live testimony, which wasn't discussed in your witness statement. This is the discipline and role of inner control unit. Yesterday, you gave a fairly lengthy answer about the role of inner control and, at the end, said that: "Inner control," and I quote you, "branch have nothing to do with disciplinary issues." That's at page 25982 of the transcript. If we could pull up Exhibit D529, please. Now, the document I'd like to show to you is an annual report of the Special Police Inner Control from 1995, addressed to General Markac, and there it discusses -- English page 2, and this is paragraph 4; and in Croatian, it's page 1. As one of the tasks carried out by inner control, and I quote the top of the English page: "Continuous monitoring of the work discipline, interpersonal relations, relations between the officers and the command structure, and pointing out the existing problems to the Special Police officers." And if we move on to page 3 of the English, at the bottom of the page, it's paragraph 4; and in Croatian, it would be page 3, also paragraph 4, the second sentence says as follows: "The section pointed out the work shortcomings, interpersonal relations, and discipline problems ..." And then if we continue in English to the next page - the Croatian is fine - we see under letter F: "Discipline in the SJP." Now, it appears from these documents that the inner control unit indeed played a role in relation to discipline. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The internal control of the Special Police Sector connected to my unit and other units had this row, and our only obligation towards them was the following: The commander drafted monthly reports, and in those he listed what had been done, what curricula parts were dealt with, what specialties were practiced. And finally there was a question as to whether that past month somebody had committed a breach of discipline. That was our only obligation, to inform them whether that transpired or not. And if it did, name the person who did it. That was only for statistical purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I accept your answer. But my focus was more on the inner control unit of the Special Police, that one of their taskings was, indeed, discipline. Do you agree with that, after having seen this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had information about a problem, they would indicate that to us, but it happened rarely. Rarely did they warn us about some breaches of discipline. The commander was the one who looked after disciplinary matters in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the commander of my Special Police unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I mean the commander you referred to in the last sentence of your answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of my unit, Mr. Ivica Mindek.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move quickly through a few other areas, and I'm sure we can finish in time. You told us yesterday, and it's also mentioned in your witness statement, that you received instructions on how to treat civilian population and property, and you had received these instructions prior to Operation Storm. Now, I understand that these instructions were given by General Markac during the meeting of 3rd August in Stari Grad. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, who was present? You told us yesterday it was the commanders of units. Was your commander present as well, or just you, as the assistant commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there together with my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the other assistant, Mr. Hovinek [phoen], was also present?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was the head of inner control, Mr. Soljic, also present?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Soljic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And Mr. Soljic is also the person who interviewed you in relation to these events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How did he conduct the interview? Were you given written questions, or did he give you a question and then you answered, and he was using a note pad, or can you briefly tell us how the interview was conducted, also keeping in mind that Mr. Djurica Franjo was there as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sat down. They asked me if I could remember, from the beginning to the end, what happened during Operation Storm. I was telling them what I remembered, and they listened to me. And there was a lady who took notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember the -- yes, I believe her name is listed here. Now, was there sometimes a moment that you couldn't remember, and Mr. Soljic reminded you of something he was also aware of because he was also present, for instance, at that 3rd August meeting? Did that happen, or did that not happen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was the only one talking, and as a result we had to correct that one mistake. I was wrong about that date, and we had to correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. You weren't the only one talking; you were the only one answering. Mr. Soljic was asking the questions, of course, orally, I take it.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no questions. Nobody asked me anything. I told them what I remembered about what had happened before Operation Storm, during the Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But there has got to be -- you're a policeman. There has got to be some guidance, you know, Tell us, you know, when you went with your unit to the Zadar-Knin Administration on the 23rd of July. I don't imagine that, you know, you were sitting there and talking all the time, and the two interviewers were totally silent. Are you saying they didn't say a word?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not saying that they didn't say a word. What I'm saying is they didn't put questions to me. They didn't tell me what to tell them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just address another substantive issue. In paragraph 3 of your witness statement, you say that, and I quote you: "If civilians are spotted in the area, we should report to the Special Police headquarter, who were supposed to organise a shelter with the regular police." Now, did you, in fact, spot civilians in the area and co-operate with the Special Police headquarter, who in turn, then, apparently contacted the regular police? Do you remember an example of this instance?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part of our march from Mount Velebit to Gracac, we did not notice any civilians. We didn't encounter anybody. However, as I told you yesterday, the first time I saw civilians together with most of my men was in the village of Mazin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what did you to with these civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN VITEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilians? They were told to stay in front of their houses and wait there. They were told that the regular police would come and pick them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate your answers. I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Waespi. An opportunity is given to the Defence of each team to put further questions to the witness. I see that this opportunity is not used by any. From Mr. Cayley, we know that he had no questions. If the other parties would want to put anything on the record in this respect, then it can be briefly done. If not, I just establish that no one -- no party uses this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Under the circumstances, Your Honour, we are not putting any questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This means, Mr. Vitez, that since the Bench has no further questions for you, that this concludes your testimony in this court. The Chamber sympathises with you as far as the reasons are concerned why it's important for you to travel back as soon as possible. We'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and we wish you a safe a trip home again and strength for the days to come. Madam Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few matters. First, Mr. Cayley, could you inform us about the result of your consultation with your client about tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've discussed the matter with my client, and he is happy to proceed tomorrow, attend court, in the absence of legal representation, although we will send a member of staff from our office to be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the -- I do know that it's an unexpected situation. Would you appreciate to have any audio or video-recording under these very special circumstances? Because this is not a standing offer that -- if so, or you could also wait until you've read the transcript and then see whether you would have any further request.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour, yes. For our purposes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we leave it to that. I put on the record that when an opportunity was given to Mr. Cayley and Mr. Cermak to leave the courtroom for consultation, that they actually left for approximately 10 minutes, the courtroom, and then returned. Then I should put on the record that the Chamber authorises the Registrar to inform the Croatian government of a small portion of what has been said in private session. It is one paragraph, and it appears on my screen as page 34, line 8 to 18. Any further matters to be raised at this very moment? If not, we adjourn, and we will resume most likely tomorrow in the afternoon of the 10th [sic] of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume most likely tomorrow, the 10th [sic] of December, at a quarter past --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the 11th tomorrow, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tomorrow is the 11th. Then the rule that the Registrar is infallible is confirmed by this exception. The hearing tomorrow is scheduled at quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to apologise to the Registrar, because he is infallible, and there was no exception. I made a clear mistake by looking at the wrong note, which I'll try not to repeat. We'll resume most likely tomorrow, the 11th of December, at 2.00, not quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom III. Whether or not we will have a hearing tomorrow will be decided by the Chamber finally tomorrow morning, and then a scheduling order will be issued. If we would not sit tomorrow, then we would resume on Monday, the 14th of December, at 9.00 in the morning, also in Courtroom III. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of December, 2009, at 2.00 p.m.
